paragraphs: When an image and accompanying text imply different answers, a multimodal model must decide which to follow. This paper separates that decision into two factors: a relatively stable preference for a modality and uncertainty specific to the current example. This distinction helps explain why observed choices cannot always be attributed to a fixed visual or textual bias.

Across the tested models and benchmarks, a modality becomes less likely to be followed as its relative preference uncertainty increases. The relationship persists with different uncertainty measures. The authors identify a balance point where neither modality is preferred, providing a way to measure bias separately from capability. Internal probing also reveals that ambiguous examples near this point produce alternating answer preferences in middle and later layers.

The framework informs supervised fine-tuning for steering preferences. In the reported experiments, easy examples with a clearly dominant modality do not generalize effectively. Targeting boundary cases is essential to the demonstrated robust alignment and reduces internal vacillation, connecting training-data selection to the model’s uncertainty.
icml-2026-beyond-fixed-biases-decoding-t.tldr: Modality choices depend on case-specific uncertainty as well as stable bias, and training on ambiguous boundary cases improves preference alignment.

paragraphs: Translating a program successfully requires preserving its behavior, but the resulting program also needs to run efficiently. The authors’ preliminary study finds that translations produced by language models often execute more slowly than human-written programs. They also find that prompt engineering alone does not remedy this problem, motivating a translation process that explicitly considers alternative implementations.

SwiftTrans uses two stages. First, MpTranslator generates diverse translation candidates through parallel in-context learning, allowing the system to explore multiple possibilities. Second, DiffSelector compares the differences among those candidates to choose a translation. Hierarchical Guidance supports candidate generation, while Ordinal Guidance helps the selection component adapt to its comparative task. The central idea is to make exploration and selection distinct, purpose-built parts of translation.

The authors extend CodeNet and F2SBench to evaluate runtime efficiency and introduce SwiftBench. Across all three benchmarks, SwiftTrans consistently improves both correctness and execution efficiency. These findings support evaluating translated code on its computational behavior as well as whether it produces the intended results.
icml-2026-bridging-functional-correctnes.tldr: SwiftTrans generates diverse code translations and compares their differences to improve both functional correctness and runtime efficiency.

paragraphs: Dimensionality reduction represents data using fewer dimensions while trying to retain a meaningful property of the original representation. The choice of what to preserve determines the method’s objective. This paper proposes preserving similarity between point distributions, making that relationship the invariant that should survive the move from the original space to a lower-dimensional one.

The authors develop a linear method designed around this invariant and describe it as computationally efficient. Their contribution therefore includes both a preservation principle and a concrete way to pursue it. They also provide a theoretical proof of feasibility for dimensionality reduction, connecting the proposed objective to a mathematically supported construction rather than presenting only an empirical procedure.

Evaluation covers benchmark datasets and single-cell expression data. The reported results support the method’s effectiveness and efficiency in those settings. Taken together, the theory and experiments establish point-distribution similarity as a usable basis for dimensionality reduction, with a linear implementation that makes the proposed principle operational.
icml-2026-dimensionality-reduction-with-.tldr: The paper introduces an efficient linear dimensionality-reduction method designed to preserve similarity between point distributions.

paragraphs: Reconstructing PET images from low counts can erase weak lesion signals. The paper attributes this wash-out to contraction in the phase space used by prevailing generative models. FlowPET instead treats reconstruction as transport that preserves volume, aiming to protect faint information through the mathematical structure of the reconstruction process.

A separable Hamiltonian system defines the model’s posterior dynamics, guaranteeing a divergence-free vector field by construction. This supplies a theoretical safeguard against probability mass collapse. The PET measurement operator also determines where the method enforces agreement with observed data and where it introduces uncertainty: consistency is imposed in the range space, while stochastic variation is confined to the unobserved null space.

The model is trained through symplectic flow matching and sampled with a symplectic leapfrog integrator. Experiments on BrainWeb, clinical pediatric data, and UDPET report better SSIM and PSNR than the compared deterministic and stochastic methods, alongside stronger recovery of low-contrast lesions. These results connect the volume-preserving design to improved reconstruction under the evaluated noisy conditions.
icml-2026-flowpet-physics-informed-sympl.tldr: FlowPET uses volume-preserving Hamiltonian dynamics and measurement consistency to improve low-count PET reconstruction and weak-lesion recovery.

paragraphs: Machine unlearning aims to remove the influence of selected training data while preserving useful behavior on retained data. This paper addresses that task for quantized neural networks. It identifies a problem with methods that teach incorrect labels: the model can become confidently wrong about the forgotten examples, which conflates forgetting with learning a replacement mistake.

Orthogonal Entropy Unlearning, or OEU, instead increases prediction uncertainty on the data to be forgotten. Maximizing entropy avoids directing the model toward a particular incorrect class. A second component handles conflicts between forgetting and retention updates. It projects the forgetting gradient onto directions orthogonal to the retain gradient, addressing directional interference that scalar gradient reweighting cannot resolve.

The utility-preservation guarantee applies under a first-order approximation, which is the stated scope of the theoretical result. Experiments show better forgetting effectiveness and retained-data accuracy than existing methods. Together, the two components frame unlearning as reducing confidence in selected information while controlling how that change affects knowledge the model should keep.
icml-2026-forget-by-uncertainty-orthogon.tldr: OEU forgets selected data by increasing uncertainty and projects forgetting updates away from directions that interfere with retained knowledge.

paragraphs: FoundObj tackles the task of separating objects within complex 3D point clouds without scene-level human annotations during training. The authors argue that existing approaches struggle beyond simple objects because their learning process lacks sufficient prior knowledge about objects. Their approach obtains that guidance from self-supervised foundation models operating on 2D and 3D information.

The framework uses an object-discovery agent that starts from superpoints, which are groups of points, and progressively merges suitable neighboring groups. Reinforcement learning guides these decisions through two reward modules. One supplies semantic feedback about object meaning, while the other supplies geometric feedback about shape and structure. These complementary signals provide a way to learn object groupings without the scene annotations the task excludes.

Across diverse benchmarks, FoundObj consistently outperforms the evaluated baselines. The authors also report strong generalization in zero-shot and long-tail settings. These findings support the potential of foundation-model rewards to extend label-free segmentation to multiple object classes and to settings where examples or familiar categories are limited.
icml-2026-foundobj-self-supervised-found.tldr: FoundObj learns to merge 3D point groups into objects using semantic and geometric rewards from self-supervised foundation models.

paragraphs: Neural-network connectivity affects how activity evolves, but large architectures can make that relationship difficult to interpret. This study examines smaller connectivity patterns, called motifs, as functional building blocks. Inspired by the variety of circuits in biological networks, the authors model 13 distinct motifs as low-dimensional components of larger artificial networks.

The theoretical analysis organizes these motifs into a three-layer hierarchy of dynamical regimes. It then shows that the proportions of motifs within this hierarchy critically shape the network’s collective dynamics. This connects local wiring patterns to behavior at the scale of the whole network: the relevant design choice includes how frequently different functional patterns appear.

The authors embed motif distributions into recurrent neural networks and show that these distributions can selectively improve robustness or flexibility. Extensive experiments support the theoretical framework. The contribution is a way to understand and potentially adjust computational properties through underlying dynamics, using distributions of small connectivity structures as a handle on larger architectural behavior.
icml-2026-functional-building-blocks-of-.tldr: The paper links 13 small connectivity motifs to collective neural dynamics and shows how their distributions can enhance RNN robustness or flexibility.

paragraphs: Online reinforcement learning faces a tension between policies that are easy to optimize and policies that can express several distinct kinds of action. Simple distributions can restrict behavior, while expressive diffusion or flow policies create optimization difficulties through inaccessible likelihoods and long sampling chains. GoRL addresses this tension by separating policy optimization from action generation.

The framework performs policy optimization in a tractable latent space. A conditional generative decoder converts those latent choices into actions, providing expressive action distributions. Training alternates between the components on two timescales, and decoder refinement is anchored to a fixed prior. This arrangement supports training expressive policies from scratch while keeping optimization in a more manageable representation.

Across the tested continuous-control tasks, GoRL consistently exceeds both unimodal and generative baselines. On HopperStand, it achieves returns above 870, more than three times the strongest baseline. On high-dimensional humanoid tasks, it exceeds the strongest non-GoRL baseline by over an order of magnitude. These empirical gains support the proposed separation of optimization and generation.
icml-2026-generative-online-reinforcemen.tldr: GoRL optimizes policies in a tractable latent space and uses a generative decoder to produce expressive actions, improving tested continuous-control performance.

paragraphs: GLEAN verifies decisions made by language-model agents using expert-curated guidelines. Its motivation is that a verifier needs both relevant domain knowledge and confidence estimates that reflect actual correctness. The framework examines an agent’s sequence of decisions, allowing its assessment to incorporate how the agent reached an answer.

At each step, GLEAN rates alignment with multiple guidelines and combines those ratings into features. Evidence accumulates across the trajectory, and Bayesian logistic regression converts it into a calibrated probability of correctness. When uncertainty remains high, the framework actively seeks more evidence by expanding guideline coverage and performing differential checks. Verification effort is therefore directed toward cases where the existing assessment is less settled.

In clinical-diagnosis experiments covering three diseases in MIMIC-IV, GLEAN surpasses the best baseline by 12% in AUROC and reduces Brier score by 50%. These results indicate improvements in distinguishing correct from incorrect decisions and in the accuracy of confidence estimates. A clinician study also recognizes the framework’s practical utility.
icml-2026-glean-guideline-grounded-evide.tldr: GLEAN accumulates guideline-based evidence and selectively investigates uncertain cases to produce better-calibrated assessments of agent decisions.

paragraphs: Graph generators can produce plausible structures while still violating rules that an application requires them to satisfy. This paper uses the discrete nature of graphs to express those rules as symbolic reasoning problems. Its framework, NSPSG, combines an unconstrained diffusion model with a projection step that brings generated graphs into compliance.

The symbolic projector uses Satisfiability Modulo Theories, or SMT, to enforce constraints while keeping graphs within the training-data distribution. To accelerate generation, the framework also employs a supervised autoregressive neural projector that approximates the symbolic reasoning process. The distinction matters: strict enforcement is attributed to the SMT-based projector, while the learned projector provides an approximation intended to improve speed.

Experiments span different constraint types and graph-generation datasets, with reported validity rates of 99%–100%. For one complex nonlinear constraint, NSPSG improves data validity by up to 43% and reaches 99% validity with comparable generation efficiency. These findings support combining learned graph generation with explicit constraint reasoning across heterogeneous requirements.
icml-2026-hard-constrained-graph-generat.tldr: NSPSG combines graph diffusion with symbolic constraint projection and a learned approximation, achieving 99%–100% validity in reported experiments.

paragraphs: Video scenes contain multiple objects whose appearances and movements need to work together. Many video-generation systems create the scene as a whole, leaving users with limited control over individual elements. HECTOR introduces a pipeline that makes those elements explicitly controllable, treating the video as a composition of separately referenced objects.

Users can provide static images, dynamic videos, or both as references for the same generation. They can also specify a trajectory for each referenced element, controlling its location, scale, and speed. This combines appearance guidance with individual motion control. The pipeline is designed to preserve the references while producing coherent videos that meet constraints involving both space and time.

The experiments report better visual quality, stronger preservation of references, and improved motion control compared with existing approaches. These findings matter because successful compositional generation requires all three: recognizable elements, requested movement, and a coherent overall result. HECTOR’s contribution is a unified way to express these requirements through mixed reference types and element-specific trajectories.
icml-2026-hector-hybrid-editable-composi.tldr: HECTOR generates videos from mixed image and video references while allowing users to control each element’s trajectory, scale, and speed.

paragraphs: In non-Markovian environments, long-range dependencies, hidden information, or memory effects make the Bellman equation only approximately valid. This paper asks which parts of the resulting learning signal fit the Bellman framework and how the remaining mismatch can guide algorithm design. It approaches these questions through the topology of state transitions.

The authors represent temporal-difference errors as a mathematical object called a 1-cochain over transitions and interpret Markov dynamics through topological integrability. A Bellman–de Rham projection then produces a Hodge-type decomposition: one component is integrable, while another captures a topological residual. This separates a signal compatible with the proposed potential-based representation from the part that does not fit it.

HodgeFlow Policy Search uses that decomposition by fitting a potential network to minimize the non-integrable projection residual. The method comes with stability and sensitivity guarantees, and numerical evaluations show significant improvements in non-Markovian reinforcement learning. The contribution ties an account of Bellman approximation error to a concrete policy-search method.
icml-2026-hodgeflow-policy-search-by-top.tldr: HodgeFlow decomposes temporal-difference signals into integrable and residual components to guide policy search in non-Markovian environments.

paragraphs: This paper investigates how vision-language models turn visual emotional cues into written emotional descriptions. The authors develop a causal attribution framework based on steering vectors and construct a specialized dataset for studying that process. Their analysis organizes emotional reasoning into three stages: adaptation, aggregation, and execution.

The main finding is a separation of functions across the network. Middle-layer attention heads gather visual emotional cues in sentiment-specific ways. Deeper layers then translate that information into narrative through pathways shared more broadly across emotions. This suggests that collecting emotional evidence and expressing it in language depend on different internal mechanisms, giving the authors distinct places to intervene.

Guided by this analysis, the method strengthens emotional information flow and increases semantic activation during inference. Experiments on MER-UniBench report significant performance improvements and fewer emotional hallucinations. The effects of these interventions also support the causal relevance of the identified circuits, connecting an interpretation of model internals to changes in the model’s generated descriptions.
icml-2026-interpreting-and-enhancing-emo.tldr: The paper identifies separate circuits for gathering and expressing visual emotion, then uses inference-time interventions to improve emotional descriptions.

paragraphs: Multimodal reasoning can lose contact with the image it is supposed to explain. Converting an image to text before reasoning may discard fine details, while joint vision-language processing can allow language to dominate the visual evidence. This paper focuses on when and how the reasoning process obtains visual information.

CSMR places a language model in control of reasoning and lets it decide when to call an independent visual perception module. Those calls acquire evidence relevant to the current task. The approach makes visual inspection a scheduled part of reasoning, so evidence acquisition can respond to what the reasoning process currently needs instead of being settled entirely by an initial image description.

Across multiple multimodal reasoning benchmarks, CSMR consistently improves zero-shot accuracy over representative baselines. Further analysis attributes the advantages primarily to the scheduling mechanism. The findings support treating the timing of visual evidence collection as a substantive design choice, alongside the capabilities of the language and perception components themselves.
icml-2026-look-on-demand-a-cognitive-sch.tldr: CSMR lets a language model request visual evidence when needed during reasoning, improving zero-shot accuracy across tested multimodal benchmarks.

paragraphs: This paper studies federated optimization problems that combine nested functions with competing minimization and maximization objectives. Their difficulty comes from the interaction of these structures while training is spread across workers. Existing algorithms converge slowly in this setting, motivating a method that improves both the amount of sampled information and the communication needed.

LS²MC-GDA combines smoothing with stochastic compositional gradients whose variance is reduced. For the theoretical analysis, the authors also introduce a stage-wise extension that bridges different ways of measuring stationarity. This extension connects the algorithm’s progress to the solution criteria used in the complexity results.

The stated sample complexity is O(κ^(3/2)/(Nε³)), and communication complexity is O(κ/ε²), where κ is the condition number, ε is the requested accuracy, and N is the worker count. These bounds improve prior theoretical dependence on conditioning and accuracy. The sample bound also gives linear speedup with worker count. Experiments support the algorithm’s effectiveness alongside these theoretical improvements.
icml-2026-ls-2-mc-gda-a-smoothed-algorit.tldr: LS²MC-GDA combines smoothing and variance reduction to improve theoretical sample and communication complexity for federated compositional minimax optimization.

paragraphs: Distributed minimax learning requires workers to coordinate updates for variables being minimized and maximized. Communicating those updates can be expensive. This paper develops a decentralized stochastic gradient descent-ascent algorithm with momentum that compresses communication and uses error feedback to account for information lost through compression.

The method introduces coefficients that balance full-precision updates against compression residuals for both variables and gradients. The central analytical difficulty is circular dependence between consensus errors and compression errors: disagreement among workers and inaccuracies from compression affect one another. The authors develop strategies to handle that dependence and establish a convergence rate for their algorithm.

The theoretical results explicitly show how the compression operator affects convergence. This matters because communication savings must be considered together with their effect on optimization progress. Extensive experiments confirm the proposed method’s efficacy. The contribution therefore combines a communication-efficient update design with an analysis of the coupled errors created when both sides of a minimax problem are compressed.
icml-2026-on-the-convergence-of-decentra.tldr: The paper develops compressed decentralized minimax optimization with error feedback and establishes how compression affects its convergence rate.

paragraphs: Generating indoor scenes becomes difficult when rooms are irregular and many spatial requirements interact. ZoneMaestro organizes this task around functional zones and their relationships. It translates high-level intent into a zone graph, giving scene generation an explicit structure for coordinating meaning and geometry across different architectural forms.

The authors create Zone-Scene-10K with explicit zone-graph annotations to support this approach. Training uses an Alternating Alignment Strategy that cycles between internalizing reasoning and Zone-Aware Group Relative Policy Optimization. The goal is to reconcile semantically rich scenes with geometrically valid arrangements without relying on external physics engines. Zone-level organization supplies the common structure around which those objectives are aligned.

The paper also defines Intricate Spatial Orchestration and introduces SCALE, a benchmark for irregular indoor spaces with dense, complex spatial relationships. Experiments report significant improvements over state-of-the-art baselines in structural coherence and adherence to intent. The authors report resolving the tension between scene density and safety in these evaluations, supporting zone-based planning for intricate layouts.
icml-2026-orchestrating-spatial-semantic.tldr: ZoneMaestro uses functional zone graphs and alternating training to generate intricate indoor scenes with improved coherence and adherence to user intent.

paragraphs: Reconstructing and understanding a scene from a long image stream can become expensive when every update revisits an expanding history. S2GS builds a semantic 3D Gaussian field incrementally. It is strictly causal: it uses no future frames and does not reprocess historical observations.

The framework separates geometry and semantics into two branches. The geometry branch updates the Gaussian representation causally. The semantic branch combines a 2D foundation vision model with a query-driven decoder that predicts object masks and identity embeddings. Query-level contrastive alignment and lightweight association with an instance memory help maintain consistent object identities over time. These components let the scene representation update geometry, appearance, and individual-object information together.

Experiments show performance matching or exceeding strong offline baselines while runtime and GPU memory grow much more slowly. S2GS processes over 1,000 frames; under the same setting, offline methods using global processing typically run out of memory around 80 frames. The result demonstrates the practical scaling benefit of incremental processing in the tested setting.
icml-2026-s2gs-streaming-semantic-gaussi.tldr: S2GS incrementally reconstructs and labels 3D scenes from image streams, maintaining object identities while substantially improving long-sequence scalability.

paragraphs: Choosing numerical precision affects the trade-off between training cost and model quality, alongside model size and dataset size. This paper develops a theoretical account of those interactions within high-dimensional sketched linear regression. It compares multiplicative quantization, whose error depends on the signal, with additive quantization, whose error is signal-independent.

The analysis identifies a difference in how the two schemes affect effective capacity. In the worst case, both introduce an additive error and reduce effective data size. Their effects on effective model size differ: multiplicative quantization preserves the full-precision model size, whereas additive quantization reduces it. Thus, treating all quantization as one generic error source misses a distinction established by this framework.

Numerical experiments validate the theoretical findings. The results provide a principled basis for reasoning jointly about precision, data, and model scale under hardware constraints. Their stated mathematical setting is linear regression, and the central contribution is explaining how different forms of quantization produce distinct scaling behavior within that setting.
icml-2026-scaling-laws-for-precision-in-.tldr: In high-dimensional linear regression, additive and multiplicative quantization have different worst-case effects on effective model capacity.

paragraphs: SCOUT addresses understanding documents at million-token scale, where processing everything can consume many tokens and dilute attention. Its starting observation is that information relevant to a particular question is typically sparse. The framework therefore seeks a subset sufficient to answer that question, treating the document as something to explore actively.

Answers are developed from a compact epistemic state: a representation of what the system currently knows, grounded in its source evidence. SCOUT diagnoses gaps in that state and alternates between coarse-to-fine exploration and anchored updates. As it gathers what the question requires, it progressively contracts the state toward query sufficiency. The question therefore guides both evidence acquisition and what information remains in the working representation.

Experiments show that SCOUT matches state-of-the-art proprietary models while reducing token consumption by up to eightfold. It also remains stable as context length increases. These findings support active, evidence-grounded exploration as a way to reduce the practical cost of long-context reasoning while preserving the evaluated answer quality.
icml-2026-scout-active-information-forag.tldr: SCOUT actively gathers question-relevant evidence from long documents, matching leading proprietary models with up to eightfold lower token consumption.

paragraphs: Editing an image with a text prompt requires changing its meaning while preserving details that should remain recognizable. Existing approaches can distort those details or add artifacts. This paper proposes coordinating the source and edited images during sampling through coupled stochastic differential equations, making their generative evolution depend on shared, correlated noise.

The coupling links the two sampling processes while allowing the edited image to move toward the requested semantics. This supplies a direct mechanism for balancing the requested change with visual similarity to the source. The method applies to pretrained generative models that can be sampled by solving an SDE, including diffusion and rectified flow models. It requires neither retraining nor auxiliary networks.

The authors report high fidelity to editing prompts together with near-pixel-level consistency with the source. These findings indicate that coordinated randomness can preserve detailed visual correspondence while supporting semantic changes. The contribution is a sampling-time control method whose applicability is defined by the model’s ability to support SDE-based sampling.
icml-2026-semantic-editing-with-coupled-.tldr: Coupled SDE sampling uses shared correlated noise to edit image semantics while preserving fine visual detail, without retraining.

paragraphs: Speculative Jacobi Decoding accelerates autoregressive image generation, but verification can be confused by ambiguous visual tokens. The authors investigate this with token visualizations. They find that individual vision tokens generally represent small, local, unclear details, making it difficult for a single token to express a definite semantic meaning.

SJD-SV changes the unit of verification from an individual token to a semantically meaningful token subsequence. It uses relationships among tokens to identify groups that carry clearer semantic information together. This addresses ambiguity at the level where it arises: deciding whether a candidate is acceptable based on an isolated visual fragment can overlook the meaning supplied by nearby tokens.

The method is designed as a plug-in for existing SJD methods and their variants. Experiments across multiple datasets show significant performance improvements after integration. The stated contribution is therefore a verification mechanism that improves existing acceleration approaches by checking meaningful groups of visual tokens, supported by analysis of why token-by-token checks encounter ambiguity.
icml-2026-sjd-sv-speculative-jacobi-deco.tldr: SJD-SV accelerates autoregressive image generation by verifying semantically meaningful token groups instead of ambiguous individual visual tokens.

paragraphs: Post-training quantization reduces the precision of model weights for efficient deployment. Learning how to round weights can be accurate but costly, while compensation-based methods offer efficiency. STLA addresses conflicts that arise when these operations are separated, including incompatible parameter updates, invalidated initial rounding assumptions, and objectives that disagree across weights.

The framework optimizes rounding within clusters while integrating the learning and compensation phases. A global objective derived from the Schur complement lets local rounding decisions account for the optimal future compensation of remaining weights. This lookahead connects a decision made now to how later adjustments can absorb its error. A Hessian-guided clustering strategy uses both diagonal and off-diagonal information to encourage error cancellation within clusters.

Experiments report a new state of the art for low-bit post-training quantization while retaining high computational efficiency. The result supports aligning rounding and compensation both in timing and across weights. STLA’s contribution is the coordinated optimization of these operations, rather than treating their decisions as independent.
icml-2026-stla-spatiotemporal-lookahead-.tldr: STLA coordinates weight rounding with future error compensation to deliver fast, accurate low-bit post-training quantization.

paragraphs: TokenSwap studies a backdoor that corrupts how vision-language models describe relationships among objects. Conventional attacks often force a repeated target output, which can make them detectable through memorized patterns and excessive confidence. Here, the model can still name the correct objects while describing their relationships incorrectly, producing what the authors call bags-of-words behavior.

The training manipulation pairs a visual trigger in selected examples with textual answers whose key tokens have swapped grammatical roles. Because these answers differ only subtly from clean examples, an adaptive token-weighted loss emphasizes the changed tokens. This strengthens the association between the trigger and relational errors without requiring the same fixed target phrase across outputs.

Experiments across multiple benchmarks and model architectures report high attack success alongside evasiveness and stealthiness. The findings expose a vulnerability in compositional understanding: correct object vocabulary can coexist with an incorrect account of who or what relates to whom. The attack’s focus on relationships broadens the behaviors that backdoor evaluation needs to examine.
icml-2026-tokenswap-backdoor-attack-on-t.tldr: TokenSwap implants a stealthy backdoor that preserves object names but corrupts their relationships in vision-language model outputs.

paragraphs: Sequence generation need not proceed from left to right. However, many flexible alternatives use a fixed-length canvas and do not learn preferences over generation order. This paper develops a probabilistic framework in which a model can learn an insertion order while also generating sequences of variable length.

The authors establish a one-to-one correspondence between insertion trajectories and permutations. This allows the data likelihood to be expressed exactly as a sum over permutations, providing a foundation for permutation-based variational training. Their Insertion Process jointly learns where to insert a token, what token to insert, and when to stop. Sequence length and construction order are therefore part of the learned generative process.

Experiments cover goal-conditioned planning and molecular string generation, domains without a canonical left-to-right structure. Learning insertion order improves both modeling quality and generalization in these evaluations. The contribution connects a precise probabilistic treatment of order with a model that can grow its output dynamically, allowing the data to guide how sequences are assembled.
icml-2026-variational-learning-for-inser.tldr: The Insertion Process learns token content, insertion position, and stopping jointly, improving generation in evaluated domains without a natural left-to-right order.
